groups.content:
The printing revolution

Before printing

  • Books were copied by monks and by professional [1].
  • Most books were written on [2], which was expensive.

Gutenberg's system

  • He created a new ink that contained [3].
  • His press was based on those used for producing [4].

The spread of printing

  • In Venice, Aldus Manutius printed cheap, portable editions of [5] texts.
  • Luther's ideas were spread through printed [6] written in German.

Long-term effects

  • Scientists were able to share identical [7] and tables of data.

groups.content:
Charles Darwin

Charles Darwin is widely regarded as an [27] figure in the history of science. As a boy, however, his school lessons held little [28] for him, and his teachers considered him an ordinary pupil. He was far more [29] by collecting objects, particularly beetles. As a scientist, he proved extremely [30], gathering evidence for more than twenty years before publishing his most famous book. He believed that his success owed more to [31] and hard work than to intelligence, and his research, such as his long study of barnacles, was remarkably [32].

groups.instruction:
Questions 33-37

Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

In boxes 33-37 on your answer sheet, write

YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer
NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer
NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this

questions.explanation: Answer: scribes Paragraph 2: books were copied 'either by monks working in monasteries or, increasingly, by professional scribes '.
Answer: parchment Paragraph 2: 'Most books were written on parchment , which was made from animal skin', and the materials were costly.
Answer: oil Paragraph 4: water-based inks did not stick to metal, so 'Gutenberg developed an ink based on oil '. Water is the trap: it was used in the old inks.
Answer: wine Paragraph 4: the press was adapted 'from the screw presses that had long been used in making wine '.
Answer: classical Paragraph 6: Aldus Manutius 'produced small, relatively cheap editions of classical texts by Greek and Roman authors, which readers could carry with them'.
Answer: pamphlets Paragraph 8: Luther and his supporters 'produced large numbers of short, inexpensive pamphlets written in German rather than Latin'.
Answer: diagrams Paragraph 10: 'researchers could share identical diagrams and tables of data'.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 2 says the materials were costly and a large volume 'might require the skins of dozens of animals', but it says nothing about the price of parchment changing over time.
Answer: FALSE Paragraph 3: ' Gutenberg was not the first person to print with movable type '; printers in China and Korea had used it earlier.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 5 gives the number of copies and the materials used, but says nothing about who bought them. Universities are only mentioned in paragraph 2, in connection with scribes.
Answer: TRUE Paragraph 5: Fust took Gutenberg to court to recover money he had lent; ' Gutenberg lost the case, and control of much of his workshop passed to Fust '.
Answer: TRUE Paragraph 8: ' printed copies spread across Germany within a few weeks '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 9 says the work 'reached its readers in printed form', but there is no information about how many copies it sold or about his other works.
Answer: D Paragraph D: melatonin is ' a hormone that signals to the body that it is time to sleep '. Growth hormone in B repairs muscles; it does not prepare the body for sleep.
Answer: F Paragraph F lists methods: ' Keeping to a regular bedtime ', a dark, cool bedroom, avoiding caffeine after midday, putting away devices and short naps.
Answer: A Paragraph A: after being knocked out, Tessa Morgan ' explained that she had slept for barely four hours the night before the race'.
Answer: C Paragraph C: players spent ten hours in bed each night, and ' their sprint times had improved and their shooting had become noticeably more accurate '.
Answer: F Paragraph F: ' Coaches and team doctors also have an important role to play ', for example helping athletes to adjust their bedtimes gradually before long journeys.
Answer: muscles Paragraph B: growth hormone 'helps to repair muscles that have been damaged during exercise'.
Answer: injury Paragraph C: young athletes who sleep fewer than eight hours 'are significantly more likely to suffer an injury '.
Answer: screens Paragraph D: 'Light from the screens of phones and tablets can delay the release of melatonin'. Caffeine also keeps people awake, but the passage does not link it to melatonin.
Answer: naps Paragraph F: 'Short naps of around twenty minutes can improve alertness without affecting night-time sleep.'

text.en: the time she recorded in the race
the reasons why she had slept badly
the advice her coach gave her after the race
how her body felt during the race
how other rowers in her team had performed

questions.explanation: Answer: B, D Paragraph A: she lay awake ' worrying about her performance ' and was ' woken early by noisy guests ' (B), and ' my arms and legs felt heavy and slow ' (D). Her time, her coach's advice and her teammates are not mentioned.

text.en: how the direction of travel affects it
which sports are most affected by it
approximately how long recovery may take
the proportion of athletes who suffer from it
a medicine that can reduce its effects

questions.explanation: Answer: A, C ' the direction of travel matters : most people find that flying east... is harder' (A), and ' it can take about one day for the body to adjust to each time zone crossed ' (C). B, D and E are not mentioned.

Answer: H (outstanding) Paragraph 1: Darwin's theory 'changed the way human beings understand the natural world' and he is described as 'someone of his importance', so he is an outstanding figure. 'an' also requires a word beginning with a vowel.
Answer: A (appeal) ' The classical languages that dominated his lessons held no interest for him. ' 'held little appeal' paraphrases 'held no interest'.
Answer: C (fascinated) ' What he enjoyed was collecting things ... above all, beetles.' 'far more fascinated by' fits both meaning and grammar; 'involved by' is not correct English.
Answer: B (persistent) Paragraph 3: his strengths were 'curiosity and persistence', and ' he spent more than twenty years gathering evidence '.
Answer: J (patience) He attributed his success to a love of science, ' great patience in reflecting on a subject over long periods ' and hard work, not to quickness of mind.

Answer: I (painstaking) ' The meticulous nature of his research is illustrated by the fact that he devoted eight years to the study of barnacles alone.' 'painstaking' = meticulous; 'rapid' contradicts eight years.
Answer: YES Paragraph 1: ' his teachers and his father considered him a very ordinary boy, rather below the common standard in intellect '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Paragraph 2 explains why Darwin abandoned medicine, but the writer says nothing about how he felt about this decision later in life.
Answer: YES Paragraph 6: ' Whether some children are simply born with special abilities remains a matter of vigorous debate, and researchers are still far from agreement. '
Answer: NOT GIVEN The final paragraph discusses how Darwin viewed his own abilities, but the passage never mentions criticism of his theory or his reaction to it.
Answer: NO Final paragraph: ' he wrote that he had no great quickness of apprehension ', and he believed 'It was character, not cleverness' that made the difference.

text.en: strict discipline from their teachers
help from other pupils in their class
an inquiring attitude towards their studies
a desire to do better than everyone else

questions.explanation: Answer: C Paragraph 7: children need ' a questioning, curious approach to their studies ', persistence and a readiness to learn from mistakes. Discipline, peer help and competition are not mentioned.

text.en: People with naturally good memories learn new techniques more easily.
Natural ability is not the main factor in developing expertise.
Physical exercise improves performance in intellectual activities.
A fixed number of hours of practice will produce an expert.

questions.explanation: Answer: B Paragraph 8: focused practice ' predicts their eventual skill far better than any early test of aptitude ', and trained ordinary students outperformed those with 'naturally superior memories' (so A is wrong). No fixed number of hours is given (D).

text.en: living in a household with both parents
attending the same school for many years
having access to well-funded sports facilities
the support of an adult who believed education was important

questions.explanation: Answer: D In almost every case there was an adult ' who valued education highly and constantly encouraged the child to keep trying '. Some pupils had moved schools several times (B), and a sports coach is only one example of such an adult (C).
